annotation.title_clean: Ethical Considerations Toward Harmonizing Human and Machine Agency in Embodied Neurotechnologies
annotation.title_en: Ethical Considerations Toward Harmonizing Human and Machine Agency in Embodied Neurotechnologies
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Berberich, N.; Cheng, G.; Giordano, J.
annotation.summary_en: Neuroethics paper arguing that AI-driven embodied neurotechnologies such as exoskeletons, neuroprostheses and BCIs should prioritise users' sense of agency over functional optimisation. Using the cross-cultural value of harmony, it proposes a balanced human–machine co-agency, emphasising intentions, balance, synchrony and context, as a bridge between engineering and ethics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Embodied neurotechnologies should prioritise users' sense of agency above functional performance.
Automation of movement creates human-machine co-agency that blurs self- and other-generated action.
Harmony (Confucian and Aristotelian) offers a normative frame for co-agency design.
Four priorities: intentions, balance, synchrony, context.
Optimality should not be the goal; a harmonious balance of human and machine agency should.
